text:
mateo: Heads up — after the Cilium 1.18 rollout to west2-gpu yesterday, model-serving pods are seeing intermittent gRPC errors and ~5-15% packet loss on east-west traffic between GPU nodes. Started ~03:20 UTC.

sre_lead: copied. Any correlation with node upgrades or kernel tweaks?

mateo: only change was the Cilium daemonset + eBPF policy opt-in. No kernel updates.

alice: can you paste a small repro (iperf/tcpdump) and cilium status output?

mateo: attaching quick logs:
```
# on gpu-node-07
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -c 100 'tcp and port 50051' -w /tmp/trace.pcap
iperf3 -s &
# on gpu-node-12
iperf3 -c gpu-node-07 -P 8 -t 20
```
Iperf shows large packet loss when MTU ~1500, good at 1200.

chen: ran `cilium monitor` for a few minutes, saw a lot of retransmits and errors about "invalid GSO size" when traffic is encapsulated. Snippet: `bpf_lxc: skb_gso_validate failed: size 65536`

bob: that screams GSO/GRO interaction with the tunnel change. Did 1.18 change tunnel header handling?

alice: yes — release notes mention optimizations that alter tunnel encapsulation alignment for Geneve/GRETAP. Default tunnel MTU calculation also changed (they now subtract an extra 40 bytes in some cases). On hosts with RDMA NICs we saw different offload behavior previously.

infra-oncall: we have RoCE NICs on the GPU fleet. If Cilium is forcing overlay encapsulation for pod-to-pod across nodes, RoCE passthrough might be broken and packets could be fragmented/invalid for offloads.

mateo: confirmed: when pods are scheduled on different GPU nodes, packets go through Geneve and hit the kernel offload path -> drops. Same-node traffic OK.

devops-bot: canary rollout to west2-gpu reported 60% of daemons at v1.18 by 03:10 UTC, automated health checks green until 03:15.

sre_lead: quick mitigation options: 1) force tunnel MTU smaller to avoid GSO reassembly issues, 2) disable GSO/GRO on the NICs (temporary), 3) roll back Cilium to 1.17.x, 4) enable direct routing / host-reachable service to avoid encapsulation for compatible nodes.

alice: try (1) first — set Cilium ConfigMap `tunnelMTU: 1400` and `kubeProxyReplacement: partial` for now. Also there's a known 1.18 bug that mishandles large GSO segments with certain NIC offloads.

chen: running a quick test: applied ConfigMap override to west2-gpu canary pods only (daemonset patch annotation). Re-ran iperf, packet loss dropped to <1% and gRPC errors stopped for 10m sample.

mateo: awesome, pushing that cluster-wide now.

bob: other note — we saw iptables conntrack entries balloon on the nodes handling the encapsulation because of retransmits; keep an eye on conntrack table sizes. `conntrack -S` showed spikes.

infra-oncall: for RDMA-sensitive workloads, we should add a scheduling predicate to avoid overlay on RoCE-backed nodes until we have a proper fix. That would preserve zero-copy paths.

mateo: filed infra-ops ticket: INFRA-3247 to add node-label-based routing policy + short-lived rollback plan.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued for Cilium -> 1.17.9 on west2-gpu if new MTU patch regresses in next 30m.

alice: follow-up action: open issue with Cilium, include tcpdump + `ip -s link` offload stats, and the `bpf_lxc` monitor traces. Also attach NIC firmware/kernel versions. There's a reported fix in their upstream branch for GSO validation.

chen: pasted command outputs in the ticket: `ethtool -k eth0` shows gso/gro on, `ip link` shows mtu 1500 on physical, geneve0 MTU computed 1474 before our override.

mateo: tl;dr: regression introduced by 1.18 tunnel/GSO interaction. Applied temporary tunnel MTU=1400 cluster-wide and scheduled policy to avoid overlay on RDMA nodes. Monitoring CPU and conntrack now. Plan: either forward-port the upstream fix or rollback if we see more regressions.

sre_lead: thanks — keep alerts on for gRPC error rate and pod-to-pod latency SLOs. If loss returns >2% for 5m, auto-rollback.

mateo: will do. I'll post a postmortem draft once we have full root cause from Cilium team. :thumbsup:

alice: small note for the runbook: add a step to check `bpf_lxc` logs and GSO validation failures; saved us a lot of time.

mateo: adding to infra runbook now.
